name: Record every visitor arriving on campus, check them against the blocklist, and issue a numbered pass
priorityReason: A person the school has barred must be stopped by the system rather than only by whoever happens to be on duty and happens to know.

goal.capability: to record who has arrived, why, and who they are here to see, and to stop anybody barred
goal.outcome: the school knows who is on the premises and why, and a barred person does not get past the desk

businessRules.rule: The visitor is not an actor. They present themselves and answer questions; the front-desk staff member is the one who uses the system.
The desk checks whether the visit was pre-registered by the person being visited, so that an expected visitor and an unexpected one are not handled identically.

The desk checks the name against the school's blocklist. A person the school has barred — a non-custodial parent, a dismissed employee — is stopped by the system rather than only by whoever happens to be on duty and happens to know.
The visit is recorded with the time in and the branch it was made at.
A numbered visitor pass is issued and recorded against the visit, so that the pass can be accounted for on the way out.
The person being visited is told that their visitor has arrived.
A refusal is recorded as well as an admission. A barred person turned away is exactly the event the school will be asked about afterwards.
A visit is never deleted. A refused visit stays on the record with its reason.
A visitor cannot be logged in against a pass already issued to somebody else. A pass in circulation is not free.

This is campus entry rather than admissions, which is why it sits here. A prospective family visiting to enquire is a visitor at the gate and an inquiry in admissions, and the two are recorded separately.
A possible match against the blocklist is shown to the desk rather than resolved automatically, since a name is not an identity and the desk can ask.

transitions.condition: The visitor returns the pass and the time out is recorded (UC-29-02).
The visit is still open at the end of the day and is closed by the security staff (UC-29-02).

basicFlow.userAction: Issues a numbered pass and records it against the visit.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Refuses a pass already in circulation, so it can be accounted for on the way out.
Records the visit with the time in and the branch it was made at.

basicFlow.userAction: Refuses entry where the visitor is barred.

departures.aspect: The system stops a barred person
departures.requirement: The blocklist check runs on every log-in and does not depend on the person on duty knowing. Where no blocklist is configured, the desk is told the visitor was not checked rather than the visitor appearing to have been cleared.
There is no visitor-facing screen. The visitor presents themselves and the desk records it.
A numbered pass cannot be issued twice at once, so an unreturned pass is visible rather than reissued.
A refused visitor is recorded as fully as an admitted one, because a barred person turned away is exactly the event the school will be asked about.
A visitor is logged in within 30 seconds, since a queue at the gate is how the desk stops using the system.
A visitor record holds personal data belonging to somebody not otherwise connected to the school, and no retention period is set for it.

openQuestions.question: Nothing in the document creates the blocklist. Who may bar a person, and on what authority?
openQuestions.assumption: Unresolved. Until it is decided the blocklist check has nothing to read.

openQuestions.question: Nothing creates the pre-registration either. Who may pre-register a visitor?
openQuestions.assumption: Unresolved, and the expected-visitor path has nothing to read.

openQuestions.question: How long does a bar last, and who lifts it?
A visitor record holds a name, a contact number and the purpose of a visit — personal data belonging to somebody not otherwise connected to the school — and no retention period is set for it.
Is any identification checked against the name given, or is the name taken as offered?
openQuestions.assumption: Taken as offered as modelled, which is why a blocklist match can only be possible rather than certain.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
